shortDescription: West African crude oil differentials held firm on Thursday, receiving broader support from growing disruptions to Middle East exports.

children: West African crude oil differentials held firm on Thursday, receiving broader support from growing disruptions to Middle East exports.
West African crude is in demand as importers seek alternative grades to disrupted Middle East supply and look to cash in on high diesel and gasoline refining margins.

The seizure of Yemen's port of Mocha by Iran-aligned Houthis on Thursday posed a further threat to Red Sea traffic, while Gulf traffic remained restricted through the Strait of Hormuz as tanker attacks in the region intensified in recent days.

Chinese independent refiners have been rushing to secure crude from West Africa, Canada and South America in recent weeks, supporting spot premiums at multi-month highs as they replace thinning Iranian and Russian supplies, trade sources and analysts said.
No new tenders for West African crude were circulated on Thursday, one trader said.
Earlier in the week, Nigerian grade Qua Iboe was heard on offer at dated Brent plus $6 and Bonga at dated plus $9, but no deals were heard at these levels.

Nigeria's upstream oil regulator has warned investors developing projects at gas-flaring sites that they risk losing their permits if progress stalls, signalling a tougher push to end routine flaring by 2030.
In other news, Glencore's former head of oil Alex Beard on Thursday pleaded not guilty to two bribery charges relating to the Swiss commodity trader's operations in West Africa.
